simple: A list of exact steps that a computer follows.
analogy: A recipe that the cook follows word for word.
precise: A set of instructions for a computer; in this course it starts as C++ source code and is turned by a compiler into an executable that the operating system can run.
source: R1 of F0-29, D1 of F0-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The text of a program, written by a person in a programming language.
analogy: The recipe written in your own handwriting on a card.
precise: The human-readable text of a program, stored in files such as hello.cpp; the compiler reads it and either reports errors or produces an executable.
source: R1 of F0-29, D1 of F0-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A program that turns the text you wrote into a program the computer can run.
analogy: A helper who rewrites your recipe in the only language the cook can read, and refuses if the recipe makes no sense.
precise: A program (here g++) that checks C++ source code against the rules of the language and translates it into machine instructions stored in an executable file; it reports errors and warnings when it cannot.
source: R4 of F0-29, D2 of F0-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The finished program file that the computer can start.
analogy: The recipe after it was rewritten for the cook: ready to use, but no longer easy for you to read.
precise: A file of machine instructions and data produced by the compiler; on the Linux build machine of this course the file tool describes it as an ELF 64-bit executable, and its first bytes are 7f 45 4c 46.
source: R4 of F0-29, D3 of F0-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The set of programs you use to turn source code into a running program.
analogy: Your kitchen tools: the same recipe needs the right pots and an oven.
precise: The compiler and the programs that work with it (and, in F0-37, the debugger). This course records the exact versions the tools print, for example "g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0".
source: R4 of F0-29, D2 of F0-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The place where every C++ program starts.
analogy: The first line of the recipe: "start here".
precise: The function named main, which the program runs first; the value it returns (0 here) becomes the exit code that the run log records.
source: R1 of F0-29, D1 of F0-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: One instruction in a program. In C++ most statements end with a semicolon.
analogy: One step of the recipe.
precise: A single instruction inside a function body, such as std::cout << "Hello"; statements run one after another, from top to bottom, unless a statement such as if or a loop changes the order.
source: R2 of F0-29, D1 of F0-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The name C++ uses for "print this on the screen".
analogy: The cook calling out loud what is happening.
precise: The standard output stream from the header <iostream>; the operator << sends text and numbers to it, and the run log captures what it printed.
source: R1 of F0-29, D1 of F0-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Text written inside double quotes in your program.
analogy: Words copied exactly onto a label.
precise: A sequence of characters between double quotes in source code, such as "Hello, world!\n"; the program uses it exactly as written.
source: R1 of F0-29, D1 of F0-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The invisible character that says "start a new line here".
analogy: Pressing the Enter key on a typewriter or keyboard.
precise: The character written '\n' in C++; without it, the next output continues on the same line (R3 shows two messages glued together).
source: R3 of F0-29, D1 of F0-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A number a program gives back when it ends. 0 means "all went well".
analogy: The cook saying "done, no problems" or "something went wrong" at the end.
precise: The value returned by main (or set when a program is stopped); run_lab.sh records it in each .log file, for example "exit code: 0".
source: R1 of F0-29 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A named place that holds a value, which can change while the program runs.
analogy: A labelled jar: the label is the name, the contents are the value.
precise: A named object with a type, for example int apples = 3; reading the name gives its current value, and assignment replaces the value.
source: R1 of F0-30, D1 of F0-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The line where you first tell the computer a variable's name and type.
analogy: Putting a new empty jar on the shelf and writing its label.
precise: A statement that introduces a name and its type, such as int apples = 3; a name must be declared before it is used (F0-36 shows the error when it is not).
source: R1 of F0-30, D1 of F0-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: To give a variable its first value at the moment you create it.
analogy: Filling the jar the moment you put it on the shelf.
precise: Giving a variable a value in its declaration (int apples = 3;). With the course flags, g++ refused to build a program that used a variable before giving it a value (R4).
source: R1 of F0-30, R4 of F0-30, D1 of F0-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Putting a new value into a variable. The old value is gone.
analogy: Emptying the jar and filling it with something new.
precise: The operator = in a statement such as apples = apples + 2; the right side is worked out first, then its value replaces the variable's old value. It is not the "is equal to" of maths; that is == (F0-32).
source: R1 of F0-30, D1 of F0-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The name C++ uses for "read what the person types".
analogy: The cook listening to an order.
precise: The standard input stream from <iostream>; the operator >> reads a value into a variable. In the lab runs the input comes from a .in file instead of a keyboard.
source: R3 of F0-30, D1 of F0-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A word that makes a variable unchangeable after its first value.
analogy: A jar with its lid glued shut: you can look, but not change what is inside.
precise: A qualifier on a declaration (const int baked = 12;); the compiler rejects any later assignment to that variable.
source: R3 of F0-30, D1 of F0-30 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The kind of value a variable can hold: whole number, decimal, true/false, letter or text.
analogy: The shape of a jar: an egg box holds eggs, a bottle holds liquids.
precise: The property of a variable or value that decides which values it can hold and which operations work on it, for example int, double, bool, char and std::string.
source: R1 of F0-31, D1 of F0-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The type for whole numbers, like 7 or -3.
analogy: A jar for whole eggs: no half eggs allowed.
precise: The basic signed integer type; on the build machine it used 4 bytes and its largest value printed as 2147483647 (R3).
source: R1 of F0-31, R3 of F0-31, D1 of F0-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The type for numbers with a decimal point, like 1.5.
analogy: A measuring jug that can hold 1.5 litres.
precise: A floating-point type; many decimals, such as 0.1, are stored only approximately, which is why 0.1 + 0.2 printed as 0.30000000000000004 with 17 digits (R2).
source: R1 of F0-31, R2 of F0-31, D1 of F0-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The type for yes/no answers: true or false.
analogy: A light switch: on or off.
precise: The Boolean type with the two values true and false; std::cout prints them as 1 and 0 unless std::boolalpha is used (R1).
source: R1 of F0-31, D1 of F0-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The type for one single character, like 'A'.
analogy: One fridge-magnet letter.
precise: A type that holds one character, written in single quotes; the character 'A' printed as the number 65 when converted to int on the build machine (R1).
source: R1 of F0-31, D1 of F0-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The type for a piece of text, like a name or a sentence.
analogy: A string of fridge-magnet letters in a row.
precise: The standard library type from <string> that holds a sequence of characters; it can be joined with + and knows its length through size() (R1, R4).
source: R1 of F0-31, R4 of F0-31, D1 of F0-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Dividing whole numbers in C++ gives a whole number: the part after the point is dropped.
analogy: Sharing 7 eggs between 2 boxes: each box gets 3 whole eggs, and 1 egg is left over.
precise: When both operands of / are integers, the result is an integer and the fractional part is discarded: 7 / 2 printed 3 and 7 % 2 printed the remainder 1 (R2).
source: R2 of F0-31, R5 of F0-31, D1 of F0-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The % sign: it gives what is left over after a whole-number division.
analogy: The egg that does not fit in the boxes.
precise: The operator % on integers; 7 % 2 printed 1 in this build (R2).
source: R2 of F0-31, D1 of F0-31 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A question with a yes or no answer that the program checks.
analogy: "Is the water boiling?" in a recipe.
precise: An expression whose value is converted to bool, used by if and by loops to decide what to do next, for example temperature < 5.
source: R1 of F0-32, D1 of F0-32 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Signs that compare two values: <, >, <=, >=, == and !=.
analogy: Holding two jars side by side to see which one has more.
precise: Operators that compare two values and give a bool. == means "is equal to" and != means "is not equal to"; a single = is assignment, which g++ flagged inside an if with the course flags (R3).
source: R2 of F0-32, R3 of F0-32, D1 of F0-32 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A way to say "only do this when the condition is true".
analogy: "If it is raining, take an umbrella."
precise: A statement that runs its block only when its condition is true; an optional else block runs otherwise, and else if chains test conditions in order until one is true (R1).
source: R1 of F0-32, D1 of F0-32 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A group of statements inside curly braces { }.
analogy: A boxed group of steps in a recipe that belong together.
precise: A sequence of statements enclosed in braces; the whole block belongs to the if, else, loop or function written in front of it.
source: R1 of F0-32, D1 of F0-32 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Words that join conditions: and (&&), or (||), not (!).
analogy: "Homework done AND it is after school."
precise: The operators && (true only if both sides are true), || (true if at least one side is true) and ! (turns true into false and false into true) (R2).
source: R2 of F0-32, D1 of F0-32 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A part of a program that repeats.
analogy: "Stir 20 times."
precise: A statement (while, for) that runs its block again and again as long as its condition is true.
source: R1 of F0-33, D1 of F0-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A loop that checks its condition before every round, and stops when it is false.
analogy: "While the timer is above zero, wait one more second."
precise: while (condition) { ... } evaluates the condition before each iteration and runs the block only while it is true (R2).
source: R2 of F0-33, D1 of F0-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A loop with a counter built in: start, keep going while, and step.
analogy: Counting your stirs out loud: "one, two, three…" up to five.
precise: for (start; condition; step) { ... } runs start once, then checks the condition before each iteration and runs step after each one (R1).
source: R1 of F0-33, D1 of F0-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: One round of a loop.
analogy: One stir of the spoon.
precise: A single execution of a loop's block.
source: R1 of F0-33, D1 of F0-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A variable that counts how many times something happened.
analogy: Counting stirs on your fingers.
precise: A variable, usually an int, that is increased (for example with ++day) on each iteration and often used in the loop's condition.
source: R1 of F0-33, D1 of F0-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A loop that never stops by itself.
analogy: A cook told "stir until the soup is purple" who keeps stirring forever.
precise: A loop whose condition never becomes false; in R4 the time limit stopped the program and the log recorded exit code 124.
source: R4 of F0-33 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A named group of steps that you can use again by calling its name.
analogy: A small recipe inside a bigger recipe: "make the sauce (see page 12)".
precise: A named block of code with a return type and parameters, for example int double_it(int number); calling it runs its body and may give back a value.
source: R1 of F0-34, D1 of F0-34 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Using a function by writing its name with round brackets.
analogy: Turning to the sauce page and following it, then coming back.
precise: An expression such as double_it(3) that runs the function body with the given arguments and then continues after the call (R1).
source: R1 of F0-34, D1 of F0-34 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A variable in a function that receives a value from the caller.
analogy: The blank in "add ___ to the pot".
precise: A variable declared in a function's parameter list; it starts as a copy of the argument when the parameter is a plain type such as int, so changing it does not change the caller's variable (R4).
source: R1 of F0-34, R4 of F0-34, D1 of F0-34 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The actual value you hand to a function when you call it.
analogy: The word you write in the blank: "add salt to the pot".
precise: An expression in a function call whose value initialises the matching parameter, such as "salt" in add_to_pot("salt").
source: R1 of F0-34, D1 of F0-34 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The answer a function gives back to the code that called it.
analogy: The sauce the helper hands back when the sauce recipe is done.
precise: The value given by a return statement; a function whose return type is not void must return a value, and g++ refused one that did not (R3).
source: R1 of F0-34, R3 of F0-34, D1 of F0-34 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The word for "this function gives nothing back".
analogy: A step like "boil the water" that does not hand you anything.
precise: The return type of a function that returns no value, such as void boil_water().
source: R1 of F0-34, D1 of F0-34 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A function that checks other functions by comparing their answers with answers you worked out by hand.
analogy: Tasting the sauce before you serve it.
precise: A function that calls the code under test with known inputs, compares the results with expected values, reports PASS or FAIL and counts failures (R2).
source: R2 of F0-34 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A list of values of the same type that can grow.
analogy: A row of numbered jars on a shelf, and you can add more jars at the end.
precise: The standard library container from <vector> that stores elements in order; size() gives the number of elements and push_back adds one at the end (R1).
source: R1 of F0-35, D1 of F0-35 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A list with a fixed number of values.
analogy: An egg box: always the same number of places.
precise: The standard library container from <array> whose size is part of its type, for example std::array<std::string, 3> (R3).
source: R3 of F0-35, D1 of F0-35 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: One value inside a list.
analogy: One jar in the row.
precise: One of the values stored in a container such as std::vector.
source: R1 of F0-35, D1 of F0-35 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The position number of an element. Counting starts at 0.
analogy: The number painted on a jar: jar 0, jar 1, jar 2.
precise: The position of an element in a container, from 0 up to size() − 1; list[0] is the first element (R1).
source: R1 of F0-35, D1 of F0-35 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A for loop that visits every element of a list, one by one, without an index.
analogy: Walking along the shelf and looking into each jar in turn.
precise: for (int score : scores) { ... } runs the block once for each element, with the loop variable holding that element (R2).
source: R2 of F0-35, D1 of F0-35 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Asking for a list position that does not exist.
analogy: Reaching for jar 3 on a shelf that has only jars 0, 1 and 2.
precise: Using an index that is not less than size(); the member function at() checks and throws std::out_of_range, which stopped the program in R4 with exit code 134.
source: R4 of F0-35, D1 of F0-35 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A message from the compiler that says it cannot build your program, and where it got stuck.
analogy: The helper saying: "I cannot rewrite this recipe; step 6 is missing its end."
precise: A diagnostic that stops compilation; g++ prints file:line:column: error: followed by a description and the source line with a marker (R2).
source: R2 of F0-36, D2 of F0-36 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A message from the compiler that says "this is allowed, but it looks like a mistake".
analogy: The helper saying: "You bought pears but never used them. Did you mean to?"
precise: A diagnostic about legal but suspicious code, enabled by flags such as -Wall and -Wextra; with -Werror ("Treat all warnings as errors", R7) every warning stops the build (R5).
source: R5 of F0-36, R7 of F0-36, D2 of F0-36 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: An extra error message caused by an earlier mistake, not by a new one.
analogy: One missing step that makes the next three steps confusing too.
precise: A diagnostic that appears only because the compiler was already confused by an earlier error; fixing the first error usually removes it, as in R3 and R6.
source: R3 of F0-36, R6 of F0-36 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A program that runs your program one step at a time, so you can look inside.
analogy: A pause button for the kitchen: everything freezes and you can look into every jar.
precise: A tool (here GNU gdb 15.1) that starts or attaches to a program, stops it at chosen places and shows the values of its variables (R3, R5).
source: R3 of F0-37, R5 of F0-37, D2 of F0-37 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A place in your program where the debugger will pause.
analogy: A sticky note on step 9: "stop here and check".
precise: A location set with the gdb command break (help text: "Set breakpoint at specified location.", R5); the program stops each time it reaches that line (R4).
source: R4 of F0-37, R5 of F0-37, D2 of F0-37 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Running exactly one more line of the program, then pausing again.
analogy: Doing one recipe step and freezing again.
precise: gdb's next runs one line and treats a function call as one line ("proceeding through subroutine calls"); step goes into the called function (R3, R5).
source: R3 of F0-37, R5 of F0-37, D2 of F0-37 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A loop that runs one time too many or one time too few.
analogy: Stirring 21 times when the recipe said 20.
precise: A bug where a boundary is wrong by one, for example i <= size() instead of i < size(); in R1 the loop reached i = 3 for a vector of size 3.
source: R1 of F0-37, R4 of F0-37 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Extra printed lines that show what the program is doing, step by step.
analogy: The cook saying each step out loud while cooking.
precise: Output added only for debugging, such as [trace] i = 3, which shows the order of events and the values of variables (R2).
source: R2 of F0-37 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A recipe that produces numbers that look random.
analogy: A very long, fixed shuffled list of numbers that you start reading at some place.
precise: An algorithm that produces a sequence of numbers from a starting value (the seed); the same seed gives the same sequence, as R3 shows with seed 2026. This course uses std::mt19937 with std::uniform_int_distribution.
source: R3 of F0-38, D2 of F0-38 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The starting number for a pseudo-random number generator.
analogy: The page where you start reading the shuffled list.
precise: The value given to a generator when it is created; with seed 2026 the game's secret was 22 in every recorded run of this build (R1, R3).
source: R1 of F0-38, R3 of F0-38 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)
